Shield 3 · Verified

Document verification — the procedure

A business doesn't become "Verified" by ticking a box. Each document is submitted, then reviewed by our team against the details on it before any badge appears.

1

Business submits official documents

The business uploads its valid trade licence, the owner's Emirates ID, and supporting documents through the secure portal.

Trade licence required
2

Our team reviews each document

We check the licence number, validity and expiry, the legal name, and that the owner's ID matches the licence — not an automatic pass.

Manual review
3

The 8-document verification layer

Beyond the basics, a structured set of up to eight documents covers licence, identity, ownership and address — each one verified or rejected on its own.

Per-document status
4

A live verification percentage is shown

The profile shows a real verification % based only on what has actually been verified — so customers see the true state, not a marketing label.

5

Expiry is monitored automatically

When a licence or document expires, the verification drops and the business is prompted to renew. A badge can't sit on an out-of-date document.

Auto expiry checks
🚫
You can't pay to skip a step.Verification reflects documents we've actually reviewed. There is no paid shortcut to a verified badge.
🛡️
Shield 2 · Team

Team verification — who's really behind the business

A name on a profile isn't enough. The "Team" shield confirms the real, identified people behind the business through Emirates ID.

1

Team members are added with their EID

The business adds each member with their Emirates ID details and document images, with consent.

2

Each identity is verified

The EID number, validity and expiry are checked and matched before a member counts toward the Team shield.

Identity match
3

Customers can see who's verified

Verified team members are shown on the public profile, so a customer knows real, identified people stand behind the work.

4

Kept current with expiry tracking

Expired IDs are flagged and must be renewed — verification stays accurate over time, not just on day one.

Ongoing
🛡️
Shield 1 · Trust Score

How the Trust Score is calculated — and why it can't be bought

The Trust Score is a single 0–100 number produced by one fixed formula. It's the same formula for every business, and money is not one of its inputs.

1

It combines real, verifiable signals

The score is built from document verification, team verification, genuine reviews and ratings, and how complete and active the profile is.

Multiple inputs
2

One locked formula for everyone

The same weighting applies to every business. No one gets a custom boost, and a higher plan does not raise the score by itself.

Same for all
3

It moves only when reality changes

Verify a document, earn a genuine review, keep your team current — the score reflects it. Let a document expire and it drops. It tracks the truth.

4

It can't be purchased

There is no option to pay to increase a Trust Score. It is earned over time through verification and real customer feedback.

No paid boosts

Genuine reviews

How we keep reviews real — and block the fakes

Ratings are only useful if they're honest. Reviews on Quvera are tied to real customers, and we actively detect and remove fake ones.

✓
Tied to a real accountA customer signs in to leave a review, so feedback comes from real people — not anonymous spam.
✓
Verified review signalsStronger reviews carry verification signals like a project tag or photo, so genuine experiences stand out.
⛔
Fake-review detectionAutomated checks flag suspicious patterns — bursts, duplicates and manipulation — for removal.
⛔
No buying or faking ratingsBusinesses cannot purchase reviews or post ratings for themselves. Manipulated reviews are taken down.
💬
Owners can reply, not eraseA business can respond to any review, but it cannot delete an honest one it simply dislikes.
🚩
Report & moderateAnyone can flag a review. Reported reviews are checked and acted on by our team.
